storyteller.name: Storyteller
storyteller.description: Warm, soothing adult storyteller who reads the book and answers the kids' questions

kid_older.name: Leo (Age 8)
kid_older.description: Curious 8-year-old who asks about the plot and loves guessing mysteries

kid_younger.name: Mia (Age 5)
kid_younger.description: Playful 5-year-old who notices funny and cute visual details, giggles and gasps

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Snuggle in for Mira and the Midnight Ticket. Mira can travel one hundred years ahead. What helpful thing might she discover?

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Maybe a bus that floats over traffic, so people can get home easily!

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: I'd make a tiny travel sound. Hummm!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Let's open our book and see what tomorrow holds.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Mira woke before midnight to a little glow beside her bed. A golden ticket lay on her slippers.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “An adventure?” she whispered.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: One arrow pointed one hundred years back; the other pointed one hundred years ahead. “The past has already happened, and I can't change it,” said Mira.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “I choose the future!”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The ticket whispered, “Home by midnight, or here you stay forever.” Mira tapped HOME, and a bright path curled around her feet.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Then we'll keep the way home ready,” she said, and stepped into tomorrow.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: Ooh, a glowing path! Can I trace it with my finger? Does it show her way home?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Yes, you can trace it in the air, or just look quietly. Mira tapped HOME to keep her way home ready. Let's pause... then follow her discovery.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: A floating bus bobbed down to meet her. Mira climbed aboard, so up it went—hum, hum, hooray!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Next stop: sky garden!” sang the driver.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Up in the garden, beans curled around railings and strawberries dangled overhead. Mira picked one ripe berry, and its sweet juice made her grin.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Tomorrow tastes lovely!” she said.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: A little robot rolled over with a watering can. “Will you help?” it asked.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Mira tipped the can, so water pattered onto a thirsty seedling. “Drip, drop, grow!” they sang.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> Those orange wheels! Can I tip pretend water with the robot? Drip, drop! Will that help the tiny plant?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: You can gently tip an imaginary can, or watch quietly. Yes, the water helps the thirsty seedling. Mira and the friendly robot are helping together.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Who made all this?” asked Mira. “People planted, planned, and helped,” said the robot.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Little things grew into big things.” Mira looked at the seedling and imagined it growing tall.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The robot gave her a seed in a tiny pouch. Mira tucked it into her pocket.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “I can help make tomorrow, too!”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The ticket gave a gentle ding. Five minutes to midnight!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Mira pressed HOME, so her bright path shone all the way to the bus. “Home, home, here I come!”

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Will she follow the bright path to the bus? What if future paths helped people find their way home?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The path shines all the way to the waiting bus, so that's a good prediction. A guiding path could help people find their way. What helpful invention would you imagine? You can think quietly... Mira has five minutes, and her route is ready.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Mira hurried along the path, and the robot rolled beside her. “Thank you for tomorrow!” she called as she climbed aboard.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The bus hummed toward her golden doorway. “Home, home, here I come!”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The bus stopped as the clock began its midnight chime. Mira stepped through the doorway—one slipper, then two!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: She was home before the last bong, and the ticket folded into a little paper star.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: In the morning, Mira planted her seed with Mama. They gave it water and a sunny place, so it could begin to grow.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Drip, drop, grow,” whispered Mira. Tomorrow could be wonderful—and today, she was home.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Could we invent pots that remind people to water? What other invention could help a little seed grow?

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: Can I open my hands like tiny leaves? Her seed has sunshine now!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Yes, open your hands slowly, or imagine little leaves. A reminder pot is a thoughtful idea; your invention can be different, too. Take a quiet moment... Water and sunshine help Mira's seed begin to grow. And Mira is home... safe and cozy.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: What little thing can we do today to help make a kinder future?

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: I could help care for a plant, like Mira and Mama.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: I could help, too. One tiny drip!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Little acts of care can grow. Subscribe and come back for our next story.
